title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
An AI image generation system was used to create non-consensual sexual imagery of a real person without her knowledge or consent. The system itself had no built-in safeguards apparent from the reporting that would have prevented this misuse, such as checks against generating sexual content or alerts to potential victims. The person using it obtained source images from private social media accounts and deliberately distributed the results through multiple anonymous accounts across multiple platforms.

This is a case of a general-purpose tool deployed with no access controls, no monitoring of outputs, and no integration with victim notification or law enforcement systems. A human review step, restrictions on sexual content generation, or platform-level detection of non-consensual imagery could each have interrupted the chain of harm. It is not established whether the AI system's terms of service prohibited this use or what, if any, detection mechanisms existed on the platforms where the images were shared.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and distributing fake obscene images of a college acquaintance. The suspect, a BTech graduate in Electronics and Communication Engineering, obtained photographs from the woman's private social media account and used artificial intelligence technology to generate explicit morphed images. He then shared this content through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook while using various email addresses to hide his identity.

The victim discovered the harassment when she received messages from anonymous Instagram accounts informing her that her altered photographs and videos were being circulated on Discord servers. She reported the matter to the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi. Investigators analyzed digital footprints and traced the connections between fake profiles to identify Bansal. During questioning, he admitted knowing the woman from college and revealed that personal resentment had motivated his actions. Police recovered his mobile phone and other digital evidence, and the investigation is continuing.
title_en: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online
